```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Fontova 2023 measured tacrolimus inside peripheral blood mononuclear cells
(PBMCs) and calcineurin (CN) activity in the same cells over a 24 h
steady-state dosing interval, first on twice-daily immediate-release
tacrolimus (TAC-IR) and again four weeks after conversion to once-daily
extended-release tacrolimus (TAC-LCP). The pharmacokinetics was analysed
non-compartmentally. The one fitted model is a naive-pooled direct inhibitory
Imax model without baseline (Hill coefficient 1) linking the intracellular
concentration to CN activity, pooled over both formulations:

$$E = E_0 \left(1 - \frac{C}{IC_{50} + C}\right)$$

where $C$ is the intracellular tacrolimus concentration (pg/million cells) and
$E$ is the percentage by which a patient's CN activity exceeds that patient's
own nadir CN activity (the paper's "% inhibition I~nadir~", Equation 2,
$100 (I_x - I_{nadir}) / I_{nadir}$). $E$ is largest with no drug and falls
towards the nadir as the concentration rises.

`Fontova_2023_tacrolimus` encodes this model. It has no PK component: the
intracellular concentration is supplied per observation row as the covariate
`CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC`.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Fontova_2023_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15051481>

# Population

Twenty-five stable adult kidney transplant recipients were enrolled at
Bellvitge University Hospital, Spain (NCT02961608, 2016-2018). They had been
transplanted at least six months earlier (median 1.84 years) and had
whole-blood tacrolimus C0 of 5-10 ng/mL at steady state; 23 completed both
intracellular profiles (Results 3.1). In the enrolled cohort (Table 1), 72%
were male, median age was 58.8 years (IQR 48.4-71.1) and median weight 73.0 kg
(IQR 62.8-79.9). Twenty (80%) were CYP3A5 \*3/\*3 non-expressers. The median
total daily dose was 3.0 mg on TAC-IR and 2.0 mg on TAC-LCP after a 1:0.7
conversion. Doses were taken fasting.

The same information is available programmatically as
`readModelDb("Fontova_2023_tacrolimus")$population`.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Model form, inhibitory Imax without baseline | `E = e0 * (1 - C / (ic50 + C))` | Methods 2.4.2 Equation 4; Results 3.4 |
| Hill coefficient | 1 (simple Imax selected over sigmoid) | Results 3.4; Discussion |
| Response definition | `100 * (I - I_nadir) / I_nadir` | Methods 2.4.1 Equation 2 |
| `le0` | log(30.4) percent | Results 3.4; Discussion |
| `lic50` | log(43.9) pg/million cells | Abstract; Results 3.4; Discussion |
| `addSd` | 0, not reported | Methods 2.4.2 names FOCE-I only |
| IIV | none (naive-pooled fit) | Methods 2.4.2 |
| Covariate `CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC` | intracellular PBMC tacrolimus | Methods 2.2; Equation 4 `C` |
| Intracellular and CN geometric-mean profiles used below | digitised | Figure 2C |
| Published NCA of intracellular tacrolimus | C0, Cmax, AUC0-24 | Table 2 |

# Concentration-response

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Fontova_2023_tacrolimus")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
e0 <- exp(ui$theta[["le0"]])
ic50 <- exp(ui$theta[["lic50"]])

# The model is algebraic (no ODE state), so a single "subject" walks the
# concentration grid; time only orders the rows.
conc_grid <- c(0, seq(1, 450, by = 1))
ev_grid <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = seq_along(conc_grid),
  evid = 0L,
  amt = 0,
  CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC = conc_grid
)
sim_grid <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_grid, keep = "CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

The closed form fixes two anchors exactly: the response is $E_0$ with no drug
and $E_0/2$ at $C = IC_{50}$. The two sides of this check use the same
parameters, so the bound is tight.

```{r anchors}
at_conc <- function(sim, conc) {
  sim$calcineurin_pct_above_nadir[match(conc, sim$CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC)]
}
stopifnot(
  abs(at_conc(sim_grid, 0) - 30.4) < 1e-8,
  abs(at_conc(sim_grid, 44) - 30.4 * 43.9 / (43.9 + 44)) < 1e-8,
  abs(e0 / 2 - 30.4 * (1 - 43.9 / (2 * 43.9))) < 1e-8
)
```

## Figure 2D and Figure 2E

Figure 2E plots the observed against the predicted response. Its predicted
values lie between about 3 and 26 percent over the observed intracellular
concentrations of about 5 to 420 pg/million cells (Figure 2D x-axis). The
model reproduces that range.

```{r fig2e-range}
pred_range <- range(at_conc(sim_grid, c(5, 420)))
pred_range
stopifnot(
  abs(pred_range[1] - 3) < 1,
  abs(pred_range[2] - 26) < 2
)
```

The solid "mean predicted" line printed in Figure 2D does not match the
reported $E_0$. Tracing the line off the figure gives the points below. A
straight-line fit of $1/E$ against $C$ recovers $IC_{50} \approx 43.5$, within
1% of the reported 43.9, but with $E_0 \approx 81$ rather than 30.4. The text value is stated twice (Results
3.4 and Discussion) and agrees with Figure 2E's predicted range. The model
therefore uses 30.4, and the Figure 2D line is treated as a plotting error
(see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r fig2d}
# Maintainers' trace of the Figure 2D solid line (percent above nadir).
fig2d_line <- data.frame(
  conc = c(10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400),
  pct = c(65.9, 51.9, 37.8, 30.0, 24.8, 18.1, 14.4, 10.2, 8.0)
)
fit_line <- lm(I(1 / pct) ~ conc, data = fig2d_line)
line_e0 <- 1 / coef(fit_line)[[1]]
line_ic50 <- coef(fit_line)[[1]] / coef(fit_line)[[2]]
c(line_e0 = line_e0, line_ic50 = line_ic50)
stopifnot(abs(line_ic50 - 43.9) / 43.9 < 0.1)

ggplot(sim_grid, aes(CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC, calcineurin_pct_above_nadir)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = "Model (E0 = 30.4, IC50 = 43.9)"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = fig2d_line,
    aes(conc, pct, colour = "Figure 2D printed line (traced)")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Intracellular tacrolimus (pg/million cells)",
    y = "CN activity above nadir (%)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model curve of Figure 2D of Fontova 2023."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Time course over the dosing interval

Figure 2C shows the geometric-mean intracellular tacrolimus and CN activity
over 24 h on each formulation. The maintainers digitised both from the figure.
The intracellular profile includes a 13.5 h point that is plotted but missing
from the Methods sampling list. Driving the model with the mean concentration
profile gives the typical response at each time.

```{r timecourse}
# Digitised from Fontova 2023 Figure 2C. Intracellular tacrolimus in
# pg/million cells (left axis); CN activity in pmol RII/min/mg protein
# (right axis).
fig2c <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~conc_IR, ~conc_LCP, ~cna_IR, ~cna_LCP,
  0,     26,       26,        280,     270,
  0.5,   38,       28,        260,     256,
  1,     62,       30.5,      247.5,   249,
  1.5,   76,       32,        237.5,   246,
  2,     76,       36,        239,     233,
  3,     63,       48,        237.5,   237.5,
  4,     57,       60,        250,     230.6,
  6,     48,       59.5,      267.5,   229,
  8,     41,       52.5,      284,     234,
  12,    31.5,     41.5,      292.5,   247.5,
  12.5,  35,       40,        267.5,   247.5,
  13,    41,       39,        261,     257.5,
  13.5,  48,       38,        251,     253,
  14,    47,       35.5,      254,     256,
  15,    50,       35,        256,     262,
  20,    32,       30,        266,     266,
  24,    27,       25.5,      283,     283
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    -time,
    names_to = c(".value", "treatment"),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = recode(treatment, IR = "TAC-IR", LCP = "TAC-LCP"),
    id = as.integer(factor(treatment))
  )

# One solve per formulation: the model has no random effects, and rxode2
# warns on a multi-subject solve without an omega matrix.
sim_tc <- lapply(split(fig2c, fig2c$treatment), function(d) {
  ev <- transmute(d, id = 1L, time, evid = 0L, amt = 0, CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC = conc)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = "CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(treatment = d$treatment[1])
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  left_join(select(fig2c, treatment, time, cna), by = c("treatment", "time"))
```

The model predicts the lowest CN activity at the intracellular peak, with no
delay. Figure 2C shows the same, and the paper reports no delay between peak
concentration and maximum inhibition (Results 3.3). Across the 17 sampling
times, the predicted response and the observed geometric-mean CN activity
should therefore rise and fall together.

```{r timecourse-check}
tc_cor <- sim_tc |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    spearman = cor(calcineurin_pct_above_nadir, cna, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(tc_cor, digits = 2, caption = "Rank correlation between the predicted response and the digitised geometric-mean CN activity.")
stopifnot(all(tc_cor$spearman > 0.5))
```

```{r timecourse-plot, fig.height = 6}
sim_tc |>
  select(treatment, time, `Model: CN activity above nadir (%)` = calcineurin_pct_above_nadir,
         `Figure 2C: CN activity (pmol RII/min/mg prot)` = cna,
         `Figure 2C: intracellular tacrolimus (pg/million cells)` = CONC_TACROLIMUS_PGMC) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(treatment, time)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after morning dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the PD time course of Figure 2C of Fontova 2023 with the model response."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The model response is a per-patient nadir-normalised percentage, while
Figure 2C plots absolute CN activity averaged over patients. The two are
compared on timing and direction, not on level. The swing of the mean CN
profile above its own minimum (about 23% on both formulations) is the same
order as $E_0 = 30.4\%$. The Discussion attributes this modest E0 to a
rate-limited CN inhibition.

# NCA of the driving profiles

The model has no PK component, so NCA here checks the digitised intracellular
input against the published NCA (Table 2). An NCA of the geometric-mean curve
is not the same as the geometric mean of per-patient NCA. Individual peaks
occur at different times and are blunted by averaging, so the curve's Cmax is
expected to fall below the published geometric-mean Cmax. AUC and the troughs
should agree closely.

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- fig2c |>
  select(id, treatment, time, conc)
stopifnot(any(conc_nca$time == 0))

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, conc ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = intervals
  )
)

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax,  ~auclast, ~tmax,
  "TAC-IR",   93.06,  1052.69,  1.53,
  "TAC-LCP",  70.65,  969.45,   6.00
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "pg/million cells", auclast = "pg/million cells*h", tmax = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Formulation" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "NCA of the digitised Figure 2C geometric-mean intracellular profile",
      "versus Fontova 2023 Table 2 (Cmax, AUC0-24: geometric means; Tmax: median).",
      "* differs by more than 20%."
    ),
    digits = 2
  )

auc_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  left_join(published, by = "treatment")
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_sim$PPORRES / auc_sim$auclast - 1) < 0.15))
```

AUC0-24 of the mean curve agrees with the published geometric means to within
a few percent on both formulations. The digitised troughs (26 and 26 pg/million
cells at 0 h; 27 and 25.5 at 24 h) match Table 2's C0 (26.78, 25.63) and C24
(27.09, 25.28). Cmax of the mean curve is below the published geometric-mean
Cmax, as expected from averaging over patients with different Tmax. The
TAC-LCP Tmax of the mean curve (4 h) is earlier than the published median of
6 h, because the mean curve is flat between 4 and 6 h.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **E0 conflict between text and Figure 2D.** The text gives E0 = 30.4%
  (Results 3.4 and Discussion), and Figure 2E's predicted values (about 3 to
  26) agree with it. The solid line printed in Figure 2D, traced above, has
  the same IC50 of 43.9 but an E0 near 81. The maintainers ruled that the text
  value applies and treat the Figure 2D line as a plotting error.
* **Residual error not reported.** The paper names the estimation method
  (FOCE-I) but not the residual-error model or its magnitude. `addSd` is held
  at 0, so simulations return the typical response.
* **No inter-individual variability.** The fit was naive-pooled, so the model
  has no random effects. The paper notes high variability in the data
  (Discussion; Figure 2D scatter) but gives no estimate of it.
* **PD-only.** Fontova 2023 did not fit a PK model; whole-blood and
  intracellular pharmacokinetics were analysed non-compartmentally. To drive
  this model from a dosing regimen, supply intracellular PBMC concentrations
  in pg/million cells from another source. Per-volume PBMC concentrations,
  such as the `Cpbmc` output of `Agergaard_2025_tacrolimus`, are on a
  different basis and cannot be converted without a per-cell volume.
* **Pooled formulations.** One model describes both TAC-IR and TAC-LCP. The
  formulation difference in CN response comes entirely from the different
  intracellular concentration-time profiles, so formulation is not a model
  covariate.
* **Digitised inputs.** The time-course and NCA sections use geometric-mean
  profiles digitised by the maintainers from Figure 2C. They serve as
  illustrations and input checks, not as published parameter values.
* **Response wording.** The paper calls the response "% inhibition
  I~nadir~", but larger values mean *less* inhibition (activity further above
  the patient's nadir). The output is named `calcineurin_pct_above_nadir` to
  avoid that inversion.
